title: Local sheaf lift of compatible affine fan basic-open maps
statement: Let $P$ be a fine sharp monoid, $X=\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathrm{mon}}P$, and $\overline{\mathcal M}_P$ its sharpened structure sheaf [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. Let $T$ be a topological space with a sheaf $\mathcal A$ of commutative monoids having sharp stalks. Suppose $\varphi:P\to\Gamma(T,\mathcal A)$ is a monoid homomorphism and $h:T\to X$ is continuous with $h(x)=\{p:\varphi(p)_x\ne0\}$. Put $V_a=h^{-1}D(a)$ and $P_a=P-\mathbf N a$. Suppose homomorphisms $\theta_a:P_a/P_a^\times\to\mathcal A(V_a)$ commute with all basic-open restrictions under [lem-trf-affine-fan-localization-sections] and satisfy $\theta_a(\operatorname{cl}(p-na))=\varphi(p)|_{V_a}$ for every $p\in P$ and $n\in\mathbf N$. Then there is a unique restriction-compatible family of homomorphisms $\psi_U:\overline{\mathcal M}_P(U)\to\mathcal A(h^{-1}U)$, for all opens $U\subseteq X$, whose map on $D(a)$ is $\theta_a$. Equivalently this is a sheaf map $h^{-1}\overline{\mathcal M}_P\to\mathcal A$. For $x\in T$ and $F_x=P\setminus h(x)$ its stalk homomorphism, under $(\overline{\mathcal M}_P)_{h(x)}=(P-F_x)/(P-F_x)^\times$, sends $\operatorname{cl}(p-f)$ to $\varphi(p)_x$ for every $p\in P$ and $f\in F_x$. This value is zero exactly when $p\in F_x$, equivalently when $\operatorname{cl}(p-f)=0$. Thus every stalk homomorphism is local.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal B=\{D(a):a\in P\}$ and $\mathcal H(U)=\mathcal A(h^{-1}U)$. The sets $D(a)$ form a basis by [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. The presheaf $\mathcal H$ is a sheaf of commutative monoids: the inverse images of an open cover cover the inverse image and preserve intersections, so the unique gluing condition for $\mathcal A$ gives exactly that for $\mathcal H$. By [lem-trf-affine-fan-localization-sections], the given $\theta_a$ are homomorphisms $\overline{\mathcal M}_P(D(a))\to\mathcal H(D(a))$. Their assumed restriction compatibility makes them a natural transformation on the basis. If two indices define the same open, compatibility in both directions identifies their maps, so this is also a family indexed by the set $\mathcal B$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.3 and 3.1.6, printed pp.98--99; identify the basic-open family and its direct-image target.

proof.text: Both $\overline{\mathcal M}_P$ and $\mathcal H$ are also sheaves in the category of commutative monoids: for a cover, the map of sections to the product over the cover is an injective homomorphism whose image is the set-theoretic equalizer, so a homomorphism into the product with image in that equalizer factors through it by a set map, which is a homomorphism because the injective homomorphism into the product reflects sums and zero. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis](a) on $X$, with coefficient category the category of commutative monoids, source $\overline{\mathcal M}_P$, target $\mathcal H$ and basis $\mathcal B$. It gives a unique sheaf morphism $\Psi:\overline{\mathcal M}_P\to\mathcal H$ restricting to every $\theta_a$, hence precisely the required family $\psi_U$. Concretely, for $s\in\overline{\mathcal M}_P(U)$, its image is the unique gluing of $\theta_a(s|_{D(a)})$ on the cover of $h^{-1}U$ by the $V_a$ with $D(a)\subseteq U$. This also covers $U=\varnothing$, whose sections have their unique possible image.

source.place: VIII proof of Lemma 3.1.8, printed p.99, the sheaf-map construction left as straightforward; basis extension is Stacks 009O (sheaves.tex, lemma-restrict-basis-equivalence), algebraic structures 009R.

proof.text: For completeness interpret the family as an inverse-image sheaf map, using the underlying sheaves of sets. By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-colimits-finite-products](a), $\Psi$ transposes uniquely to $\alpha:h^{-1}\overline{\mathcal M}_P\to\mathcal A$. Give the inverse-image set sheaf its monoid operations by applying $h^{-1}$ to addition and zero, using the finite-product comparisons in clause (b) of that node; the monoid identities follow by functoriality. Indeed $\Psi=h_*\alpha\circ\eta$ and $\eta$ respects the product comparisons. Thus the two maps $\alpha\circ h^{-1}(+)$ and $+\circ(\alpha\times\alpha)$ have adjuncts $\Psi\circ+$ and $+\circ(\Psi\times\Psi)$, respectively; these agree since $\Psi$ preserves addition. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves the required equality; zero is the same argument with the terminal sheaf. Conversely these equations transpose back. Thus this is a bijection of monoid sheaf maps, not merely set maps. By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-stalk], the canonical bijection from the source stalk at $h(x)$ to the inverse-image stalk at $x$ sends $s_{h(x)}$ to the germ of its pullback. It preserves addition and zero because those operations are defined by these same pullbacks. Consequently the stalk homomorphism induced by $\alpha$ sends $s_{h(x)}$ to $(\psi_U(s))_x$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.6 and proof of Lemma 3.1.8, printed p.99; underlying-set adjunction and germ convention: Stacks 008H (sheaves.tex, lemma-stalk-pullback).

proof.text: Fix $x\in T$, put $\mathfrak p=h(x)$ and $F_x=P\setminus\mathfrak p$. For $p\in P$ and $f\in F_x$, one has $\mathfrak p\in D(f)$, hence $x\in V_f$. The class $\operatorname{cl}(p-f)$ is a section on $D(f)$. Its germ corresponds to the same class in $(P-F_x)/(P-F_x)^\times$ by [lem-trf-affine-fan-localization-sections]. Since $\psi_{D(f)}=\theta_f$, the assumed numerator formula with $a=f,n=1$ sends this germ to $(\varphi(p)|_{V_f})_x=\varphi(p)_x$. Every element of the localized monoid is of the form $p-f$, so this computes the entire stalk map.

source.place: VIII 3.1.2--3.1.3 and proof of Lemma 3.1.8(i)--(ii), printed pp.98--99; compute the local factor on a fraction.

proof.text: By the hypothesis defining $h$, $\varphi(p)_x=0$ if and only if $p\notin h(x)$, that is $p\in F_x$. In $P-F_x$ the element $f$ is a unit, so $\operatorname{cl}(p-f)=\operatorname{cl}(p)$. The final clause of [lem-trf-affine-fan-localization-sections] says that this last class is zero exactly when $p\notin h(x)$. The sharpening of a monoid is sharp: if the classes of $u,v$ sum to zero, then $u+v$ is a unit; choosing its inverse $w$ shows $u+(v+w)=0$, so $u$ is a unit and its class is zero. Thus the source stalk has only the unit zero; the target stalk has only the unit zero by hypothesis. The computed map has zero inverse image exactly zero, hence is local by [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup].
